classification.difficultyReason: Part a is signposted: ignore (1,1) and sketch a line through the remaining falling trend, the same by-eye skill as p11-q1. Part b is the hardest essential demand. The student must include the outlier and judge how it pulls the line, producing a less steep line with points balanced either side. This needs more judgement than p11-q1's plain sketches. It is still a drawing task with no explanation or written reasoning. That keeps it below p12-q4, which asks the student to state the outlier's effect on the gradient.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a line of best fit that ignores the point $(1,1)$.

answer.short: A downward-sloping straight line through the middle of the eight points on the right, for example from $(1.5,8.6)$ to $(9,1.5)$.
answer.worked: Ignore $(1,1)$. The other eight points fall steadily, so draw a straight line close to them with points above and below it. One example passes approximately through $(1.5,8.6)$ and $(9,1.5)$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Draw a line of best fit for all nine points.

answer.short: A downward-sloping straight line that is less steep than in part a, for example from $(1,6)$ to $(9,3)$.
answer.worked: Now $(1,1)$ must be taken into account. It lies far below the other points, so it pulls the left end of the line down. The line is less steep than in part a. One example passes approximately through $(1,6)$ and $(9,3)$.
